source.book: Tajweed Rules of the Qur'an — Part One
source.verification: book source checked; Qur'anic references cross-checked

prerequisites: Understand that idgham merges the target into the following letter.
Identify idgham with ghunnah in ي ن م و.
learningOutcomes: Name lam and ra as the two letters of idgham without ghunnah.
Identify the rule after noon saakinah or tanween.
Contrast ي ن م و with ل ر.
Explain that no two-count idgham ghunnah remains with lam or ra.
Recite verified examples by merging directly into lam or ra.

linguistic.ar: الإدغام هو إدخال حرف في حرف حتى يصيرا كحرف واحد مشدد.
linguistic.en: Idgham means merging one letter into another until they sound like one strengthened letter.

technical.ar: الإدغام بغير غنة هو إدخال النون الساكنة أو التنوين في اللام أو الراء إذا جاء أحدهما في أول الكلمة التالية، من غير إبقاء غنة الإدغام.
technical.en: Idgham without ghunnah merges noon saakinah or tanween into lam or ra at the beginning of the next word, without retaining the idgham ghunnah.

studentFriendly.ar: إذا جاء بعد النون الساكنة أو التنوين لام أو راء في الكلمة التالية، ندمج صوت النون مباشرة في اللام أو الراء بلا غنة حركتين.
studentFriendly.en: If lam or ra begins the next word after noon saakinah or tanween, merge directly into it without a two-count ghunnah.

definition.memoryFormula: نْ أو تنوين + ل ر = إدغام بغير غنة

keyTerms.en: complete merging; detailed further in the next lesson

teacherPreparation: Prepare trigger cards ل and ر.
Place ينمو and ل ر in two contrasting columns.
Model an incorrect nasal hold, then the correct direct merge.
Listen for smooth entry into the strengthened lam or ra.

openingReview.teacherPrompt: Ask the learner to name ينمو and its ghunnah timing.
Show ل and ر and ask whether they belong to ينمو.
Review that idgham occurs across two words.

conceptExplanation.text: Both kinds of idgham merge the noon sound. The difference is what remains: with ينمو we keep a two-count ghunnah; with lam and ra we merge without that ghunnah.
Avoid saying that all nasal resonance can be physically removed; teach the practical recitation distinction as transmitted and assess it by listening.

visualExplanation.teacherUse: Keep ل ر visually separate from ينمو.

ruleSummary.condition: Noon saakinah or tanween is followed in the next word by lam or ra.
ruleSummary.result: Merge directly into lam or ra without retaining a two-count idgham ghunnah.

quranExamples.readingInstruction: Merge noon directly into the strengthened ra without a two-count ghunnah.
quranExamples.teacherExplanation: Ra begins the next word after noon saakinah.
quranExamples.commonError: Holding a nasal sound before ra.

quranExamples.arabic: قَيِّمًا لِّيُنذِرَ بَأْسًا شَدِيدًا مِّن لَّدُنْهُ
quranExamples.readingInstruction: Merge noon into the strengthened lam with no two-count nasal hold.
quranExamples.commonError: Pronouncing a separate noon before lam.

quranExamples.readingInstruction: Merge the tanween noon sound directly into lam.
quranExamples.teacherExplanation: Lam follows tanween across two words.
quranExamples.commonError: Keeping the tanween noon separate or adding a two-count ghunnah.

quranExamples.readingInstruction: Merge the tanween noon sound into the strengthened ra without a two-count ghunnah.
quranExamples.teacherExplanation: Ra follows tanween across two words.
quranExamples.commonError: Adding the same ghunnah used with ي ن م و.

guidedPractice.teacherAction: Display the target and trigger only.
guidedPractice.studentAction: Classify the trigger as ينمو or ل ر.
guidedPractice.feedback: Require the learner to state whether ghunnah remains.

guidedPractice.teacherAction: Model direct entry into lam or ra.
guidedPractice.studentAction: Isolate the boundary, merge, then recite the phrase.
guidedPractice.feedback: Correct a separate noon and an added nasal hold independently.

instruction.en: Which letters cause idgham without ghunnah?

items: ء ه ع ح غ خ
interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Lam and ra form this group.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: Keep ل ر separate from the memory word ينمو.

instruction.en: Which group keeps a two-count ghunnah?

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. The two-count idgham ghunnah belongs to ينمو.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: Lam and ra are taught without retaining that ghunnah.

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Ra begins the next word.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: Find the first letter after the target.
Inspect the beginning of the second word.
The trigger begins the following word.
Ra belongs to the ل ر group.
Compare waw with the two groups.

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Ayn is a throat letter.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: Ayn is not in ينمو or ل ر.

instruction.en: A learner holds a two-count ghunnah before ra. What should change?

items: Merge directly without the two-count hold
acceptedAnswers: Merge directly without the two-count hold
interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Enter directly into the strengthened ra.

instruction.en: A learner pronounces noon clearly before lam. What is the correction?

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. The noon should not remain separate.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: Idgham requires merging into the trigger.

interactiveActivities.prompt: Noon saakinah or tanween + ل ر = …
interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Lam and ra are the two letters.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: Recall the separate group ل ر.

interactiveActivities.prompt: How do ينمو and ل ر differ?
items: Both merge, but only ينمو keeps the two-count ghunnah
acceptedAnswers: Both merge, but only ينمو keeps the two-count ghunnah
interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Excellent. You identified the shared action and key difference.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: Both are idgham; compare what happens to ghunnah.

commonMistakes: Adding a two-count ghunnah before lam or ra.
Confusing ل ر with the ينمو group.
Forgetting that the trigger begins the next word.
correctionTechniques: Use two columns: ينمو with ghunnah and ل ر without it.
Practice direct boundary pairs before full phrases.
Contrast رحيمٌ ودودٌ with غفورٌ رحيمٌ.
Ask the learner to name the group before reciting.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Recite one lam and one ra example.

teacherQuestions: Does lam or ra begin the next word?
Does a two-count idgham ghunnah remain?
studentTasks: Sort triggers into ينمو and ل ر.
Compare one example from each idgham type.
independentPractice: Make two trigger columns: ينمو and ل ر.
Mark one lam and one ra example.
homework: Prepare two lam and two ra examples approved by the teacher.
Explain the difference from idgham with ghunnah before reciting.
exitTicket: Recite one example without an added two-count ghunnah.
masteryCriteria: Identifies the rule in at least 8 of 10 mixed items.
Contrasts the two idgham groups correctly.
teacherNotes: Assess the practical distinction by listening, not only verbal explanation.
The next lesson will refine complete and incomplete idgham terminology.
Keep the two idgham groups visible during mixed practice.
